name: Philemon
overview: Philemon is a male believer recognized as a fellow worker with the Apostle Paul, as noted in Paul's letter addressed to him. He is the recipient of this epistle, indicating his significance within the early Christian community. Beyond his association with Paul, Scripture does not provide further details about his tribe or background.
namesAndTitles: Philemon is the sole name recorded for this individual, with no specific meaning or title given in the biblical text. The name appears in the context of Paul's letter to him, simply identifying him without additional name-based significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Philemon beyond his role as a fellow worker with Paul. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Philemon's importance in the New Testament lies in his partnership with Paul in ministry, highlighting a close working relationship in advancing the gospel. The letter addressed to him underscores his role within the early church and reflects the personal nature of Paul's ministry. His mention as a fellow worker emphasizes the collaborative effort in spreading Christ-centered faith.
